We all want calls to support our teams, not hurt them, but even I can watch a CFB game and tell when a call against my team is good or bad. False starts are easy to tell, holding penalties happen every down so it's really just a matter of time before one gets called. I hate it when my team gets caught for a block in the back or a pass interference, but I certainly don't think my team is incapable of doing wrong. I'd like to think I'm pretty fair in my assessment of rule-breaking on the field of play.

But last night...that might have been the worst called game I've ever seen.

The mainstream media isn't saying a thing, but chatboards were blowing up last night, and anyone watching live could tell the refs were not calling a fair game. Let me clarify:

  • No call - TAMU linebacker (Reggie Chevis) got beat and was faceguarding Ardarius Stewart on a goal line catch, ruled incomplete. The rule states that a defensive player cannot have his back to the ball and put his hands in the face of a receiver attempting to make the catch. The defender must make a play on the ball for contact/faceguarding to be allowed.

  • No call - Blatant late hit on Ridley, who had just been called down 2 seconds earlier. Not only was the play over, but his head was turned because he had been heading out of bounds during the play anyway.

  • No call - Marlon Humphrey's interception, ruled incomplete. His feet were in-bounds before playing the ball, and he remained in-bounds while establishing possession (which he maintained on the way out-of-bounds).

  • No call - Horrific facemask on Coker as he ran out-of-bounds, the official was standing 3-yards away. It happened right in front of Saban, and I thought was going to have an aneurysm. It straight up looked like Coker's head had been ripped off his torso. Apparently, the way to get that call in Kyle Field is for the defender to be holding the evidence in his hand like a member of ISIS.

  • No call - Block in the back on a punt return. I can't remember when/where, but I remember being angry about it because I believe it was a clear and easy call that was overturned.

  • No call - Personal foul, a TAMU defensive end headbutted/speared Coker's facemask after he got up following an out-of-bounds scramble. Again, it's after the play, so officials are running over to get the ball and mark off the new LoS. This was a big missed call.

  • Ejection for targeting (4:59 in 2nd) - While it's clear that Hamilton made helmet-to-helmet contact, my first gripe is that the refs missed at least three targeting calls on TAMU. One was obvious because their player left his feet while hitting our defenseless QB in the face (QBs are supposed to have their own ref), and Justin Evans hit Derrick Henry several times head-to-head. My second gripe is that it's a ridiculous call anyway, and ejecting a player for it is downright absurd. Helmet-to-helmet contact happens on every single play, somewhere on the field, and being selective about when and where you call it creates a lot of problems for officiating. This game is a great example of that.

  • Pass interference call in the endzone - This was overturned (because the replay showed the refs just how idiotic the call was). The replay also shows a line judge STANDING RIGHT UNDER THE BALL AS IT FLIES OVER HIS HEAD - clearly uncatchable, and the WR fell over anyway so it was a poor call to begin with. It's a shame that it took irrefutable video evidence to guilt them into changing a bad call.

  • Countless scrimmage no calls - This is something that you had to watch live to really appreciate, and I'll be the first to admit that most activity along the line of scrimmage doesn't get called often. If every hands-to-the-face, holding (off and def), and neutral zone infraction was called, CFB games would last 4-5 hours. However, you can't tell me that a middling offensive line can go an entire game without a single holding penalty on the best defensive front in the country. So, while I'm ok not getting calls every time, I saw many that deserved acknowledgment.

Even Danny Kanell, who I have no love for at all, was tweeting about how bad the officiating was in the Alabama-TAMU game, and was one of a million people who disagreed with the targeting call. Hell, even Gary Danielson, the biggest derping color guy in college football, noticed a disproportionate amount of calls against Alabama during the game. Unsurprisingly, fatface Verne Lundquist didn't seem to mind.

It was just ridiculous. Texas A&M had only a single penalty called on them the entire game - a false start at the 13:50 mark in the 2nd Quarter. Meanwhile, Alabama is smacked with administrative stuff, like the substitution penalty literally 5 seconds before that, and an illegal motion penalty later in the game (despite the fact that we were set and on the line of scrimmage). Bama finished with 7 penalties for 60 yards, but it would've been more like 9 or 10 for 80-90 yards because TAMU declined a few.
Alabama vs Texas A&M: The worst officiating of 2015

The state of officiating in general seems to be on the decline. The Big XII has had several game-changing bad calls of late, and the league just shrugs it off.

Officials should be suspended like they are in the NFL when blown calls affect the outcome of the game.
